pivotalTrials.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase in Stroke Patients Selected by Perfusion Mismatch (TASTE): A Multicentre, Phase 3 RCT
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Tenecteplase was non-inferior to alteplase in perfusion-selected stroke patients within 4.5h, with numerically higher early reperfusion in large vessel occlusions.

primaryEndpoint.metric: Substantial early neurological improvement (NIHSS reduction ≥8 or reaching 0–1 at 24h)
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 56.8% vs. 50.1% (adjusted RR 1.13, 95% CI 0.98–1.30; non-inferior, p<0.001)

pico.population: AIS with occlusion of ICA or MCA-M1/M2 presenting 4.5 to 24 hours from onset with salvageable penumbral mismatch on perfusion imaging
pico.timeWindow: 4.5 to 24 hours from last known well (penumbral mismatch on CTP/MRP)
pico.intervention: IV Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg bolus

pivotalTrials.title: Tenecteplase in Stroke at 4.5 to 24 Hours with Salvageable Penumbra (TIMELESS)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: In patients presenting 4.5 to 24 hours with LVO receiving endovascular therapy, IV tenecteplase did not significantly shift 90-day functional recovery, but demonstrated acceptable safety without excess sICH.

primaryEndpoint.metric: mRS score distribution (shift analysis) at 90 days
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Median mRS 3 vs. 3 (adjusted common OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.82–1.57; p=0.45)

pico.population: Adults with anterior circulation LVO and ASPECTS 3–5 or infarct core volume 70–100 mL
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 24 hours from symptom onset (large core: ASPECTS 3–5 or infarct vol 70–100 mL)
pico.intervention: Endovascular thrombectomy + medical management

pivotalTrials.title: Study of Endovascular Therapy in Acute Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusive Patients With a Large Infarct Core (ANGEL-ASPECT)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Demonstrates robust functional recovery with EVT in large ischemic core (ASPECTS 3–5 or 70–100 mL) within 24 hours.

pico.comparator: IV Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg followed by standard antiplatelet therapy after 24h
pico.population: Patients with acute minor nondisabling ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤5 with ≤1 in individual domains) within 4.5h
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4.5 hours from onset (minor non-disabling AIS: DAPT vs Alteplase)
pico.intervention: DAPT (Clopidogrel 300 mg load + Aspirin 100 mg for 14 days, then clopidogrel monotherapy)

pivotalTrials.title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy vs Alteplase for Patients With Minor Nondisabling Acute Ischemic Stroke (ARAMIS)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: For acute minor non-disabling ischemic stroke presenting within 4.5h, early DAPT was non-inferior to IV alteplase and avoided hemorrhagic transformation risks, establishing DAPT as the preferred standard (Class 3: No Benefit for IVT).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: 0.3% vs. 0.9% (no sICH in DAPT arm; lower bleeding risk)

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 93.8% vs. 91.4% (adjusted difference 2.3%, 95% CI -1.5% to 6.2%; met noninferiority margin -4.5%)

pico.population: Patients 18 to 70 years with large hemispheric infarction (ASPECTS 1–5 or DWI lesion 80–300 mL) within 10h
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 10 hours from symptom onset (Cirara/IV glibenclamide for large hemispheric infarction)
pico.intervention: Continuous IV Glibenclamide (BIIB093, SUR1-TRPM4 channel inhibitor) for 72 hours

pivotalTrials.title: Cirara for Hemispheric Infarction with Severe Edema (CHARM): A Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trial
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: IV glibenclamide did not significantly improve 90-day functional independence in large hemispheric infarction; routine medical treatment to prevent cerebral edema with glibenclamide is NOT recommended (Class 3: No Benefit).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: All-cause mortality was numerically reduced (21.7% vs 27.5%; HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.55–1.04)

primaryEndpoint.metric: mRS shift analysis across 90-day disability levels
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Adjusted common OR 1.12 (95% CI 0.84–1.49; p=0.45; no significant functional improvement)

pico.comparator: Later guideline-based DOAC initiation (day 3–4 minor, day 6–7 moderate, day 12–14 major)
pico.population: AIS patients with atrial fibrillation stratified by infarct size (minor, moderate, major on imaging)
pico.timeWindow: Early DOAC initiation: ≤ 48h (minor stroke), Day 3–4 (moderate), Day 6–7 (major)
pico.intervention: Early DOAC initiation (<48h minor/moderate, day 6–7 major)

pivotalTrials.title: Early versus Later Anticoagulation for Stroke with Atrial Fibrillation (ELAN)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Early infarct-size-guided DOAC initiation after AF-related ischemic stroke is safe (0.2% sICH) and lowers early recurrent stroke risk.

primaryEndpoint.metric: 30-day composite of recurrent ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, major extracranial bleeding, sICH, or vascular death
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 2.9% vs. 4.1% (risk difference -1.18%, 95% CI -2.84 to 0.47)

pico.population: Patients with mild ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤5) or high-risk TIA with presumed atherosclerotic cause presenting within 24 to 72 hours from onset
pico.timeWindow: 24 to 72 hours from symptom onset (delayed DAPT initiation)
pico.intervention: Clopidogrel (300 mg load, then 75 mg/day) + Aspirin for 21 days, followed by clopidogrel monotherapy

pivotalTrials.title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Initiated within 72 Hours after Minor Stroke or TIA (INSPIRES)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Extended the time window for starting DAPT: initiating clopidogrel plus aspirin within 24 to 72 hours of mild stroke or TIA of atherosclerotic origin significantly prevents 90-day recurrent stroke (Class 2a, LOE B-R).

primaryEndpoint.metric: New ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke within 90 days
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 7.3% vs. 9.2% (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.66–0.94; p=0.008; 21% relative reduction)

pico.population: AIS patients achieving successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b–3) after EVT
pico.timeWindow: First 24h post-successful EVT (intensive SBP < 140 mmHg vs conventional 140–180 mmHg)
pico.intervention: Intensive BP management (SBP <140 mmHg for 24h)

pivotalTrials.title: Intensive vs Conventional Blood Pressure Management After Thrombectomy in Acute Ischemic Stroke (OPTIMAL-BP)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Targeting SBP <140 mmHg after successful EVT significantly lowers the likelihood of functional independence compared with 140–180 mmHg.

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 39.4% vs. 54.4% (adjusted OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.33–0.96, p=0.03; terminated early for harm)

pico.population: AIS patients presenting within 4.5h of onset not planned for endovascular therapy
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4.5 hours from symptom onset
pico.intervention: IV Mutant Recombinant Prourokinase (rhPro-UK 35 mg single infusion)

pivotalTrials.title: Efficacy and Safety of Recombinant Human Prourokinase in Acute Ischemic Stroke (PROST): A Randomized Phase 3 Noninferiority Trial
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Recombinant prourokinase demonstrated non-inferiority for 90-day functional recovery compared with alteplase with lower systemic bleeding and sICH rates (Class 2b, LOE B-R).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: 1.2% vs. 2.7% (significantly lower bleeding with rhPro-UK; p=0.04)

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 68.2% vs. 64.9% (difference 3.3%, 95% CI -1.8% to 8.4%; met noninferiority margin -8%)

pico.population: Adults with anterior LVO (ICA or M1) and large ischemic core (ASPECTS 3–5 or CTP core ≥50 mL)
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 24 hours from last known well (large core: ASPECTS 3–5 or core ≥ 50 mL)
pico.intervention: Endovascular thrombectomy + medical care

pivotalTrials.title: Trial of Endovascular Thrombectomy for Large Ischemic Strokes (SELECT2)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Endovascular thrombectomy significantly improves functional independence in anterior LVO patients with large core (ASPECTS 3–5) up to 24h.

primaryEndpoint.metric: 90-day ordinal mRS shift (generalized OR) & functional independence (mRS 0–2)

pico.population: AIS with anterior LVO and ASPECTS 3–5 selected predominantly by non-contrast CT (without mandatory perfusion)
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 12 hours from symptom onset or wake-up stroke (ASPECTS 3–5 on NCCT/MRI)
pico.intervention: Endovascular thrombectomy + medical treatment

pivotalTrials.title: Efficacy and Safety of Thrombectomy in Stroke With Extended Lesion and Extended Time Window (TENSION)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: NCCT-based selection of ASPECTS 3–5 patients for EVT significantly improves functional outcome and reduces mortality without requiring CT perfusion.

pico.population: Adults with AIS (NIHSS 5–25) eligible for IVT but ineligible for or declining EVT
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4.5 hours from symptom onset
pico.intervention: IV Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg bolus (max 25 mg)

pivotalTrials.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase in Acute Ischaemic Cerebrovascular Events (TRACE-2)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Confirms non-inferior efficacy and comparable safety of Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg vs. Alteplase in AIS within 4.5 hours.

pico.comparator: IV Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (10% bolus + 60-min infusion, max 90 mg)
pico.population: Adults ≥18y with disabling AIS eligible for standard IV thrombolysis
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4.5 hours from symptom onset
pico.intervention: IV Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg single bolus (max 25 mg)

pivotalTrials.title: Intravenous Tenecteplase Compared With Alteplase for Acute Ischaemic Stroke in Canada (AcT)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg is non-inferior to Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg for all IVT-eligible AIS patients within 4.5h with rapid single-bolus workflow advantage.

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 36.9% vs. 34.8% (unadjusted RD 2.1%, 95% CI -2.6 to 6.9; met non-inferiority)

pico.population: Adults with moderate-to-severe Basilar Artery Occlusion (NIHSS ≥10, PC-ASPECTS ≥6)
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 12 hours of estimated basilar artery occlusion onset
pico.intervention: Endovascular thrombectomy + best medical care

pivotalTrials.title: Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar-Artery Occlusion (ATTENTION)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Endovascular thrombectomy doubles good functional outcomes and cuts mortality by one-third in basilar artery occlusion (NIHSS ≥10).

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 46% vs. 23% (adjusted rate ratio 2.06, 95% CI 1.46–2.91, p<0.001)

pico.population: Basilar artery occlusion presenting 6–24 hours from symptom onset
pico.timeWindow: 6 to 24 hours from basilar artery occlusion onset
pico.intervention: Thrombectomy + standard medical therapy

pivotalTrials.title: Trial of Thrombectomy 6 to 24 Hours after Stroke Due to Basilar-Artery Occlusion (BAOCHE)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Confirms efficacy of late-window (6–24h) mechanical thrombectomy in basilar artery occlusion.

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 46% vs. 24% (adjusted rate ratio 1.81, 95% CI 1.26–2.60, p<0.001)

pico.population: AIS patients with anterior circulation LVO who achieved successful mechanical recanalization (mTICI 2b, 2c, or 3) within 24h
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 24 hours from onset (adjunctive intra-arterial Alteplase post-EVT reperfusion)
pico.intervention: Adjunctive intraarterial alteplase (0.225 mg/kg infused over 15–30 min)

pivotalTrials.title: Effect of Intra-arterial Alteplase vs Placebo Following Successful Thrombectomy on Functional Outcomes in Patients With Large Vessel Occlusion Acute Ischemic Stroke (CHOICE)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Adjunctive intraarterial thrombolysis after successful EVT to clear microvascular thrombosis may improve 90-day excellent functional outcome without increasing sICH (Class 2b, LOE B-R).

pico.population: Adults with persistent hypertension (SBP ≥140 mmHg) after successful mechanical thrombectomy (eTICI 2b–3)
pico.timeWindow: Post-reperfusion (first 72 hours post-successful EVT; SBP target < 120 mmHg harmful)
pico.intervention: Intensive SBP target <120 mmHg

pivotalTrials.title: Intensive Blood Pressure Control After Endovascular Thrombectomy for Acute Ischaemic Stroke (ENCHANTED2/MT)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Intensive SBP lowering (<120–140 mmHg) after successful EVT causes worse functional outcomes and is NOT recommended (Class III: Harm).

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Common OR for worse mRS: 1.37 (95% CI 1.07–1.76, p=0.01); trial stopped early for harm

pico.population: Adults with moderate-to-severe AIS (NIHSS ≥6) within 4.5h
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4.5 hours from symptom onset
pico.intervention: IV Tenecteplase 0.4 mg/kg high-dose bolus (max 40 mg)

pivotalTrials.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase for Management of Acute Ischaemic Stroke (NOR-TEST 2, Part A): A Randomised, Controlled Trial
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: High-dose tenecteplase (0.4 mg/kg) caused significantly worse functional outcomes, increased mortality, and higher sICH. It is strongly NOT recommended (Class 3: No Benefit / Harm).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: 6% vs. 1% (OR 6.64, 95% CI 0.79–56.1; excess hemorrhage in 0.4 mg/kg arm)

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 32% vs. 51% (adjusted OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.25–0.81; trial stopped early for safety)

pico.comparator: Initial transport to closest Local Primary Stroke Center (PSC) with secondary transfer if needed
pico.population: Patients with acute stroke and RACE scale score >4 (suspected LVO) evaluated by EMS in Catalonia
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 7 hours from symptom onset (prehospital direct-to-EVT triage)
pico.intervention: Direct bypass transfer to distant Comprehensive/Thrombectomy Stroke Center (TSC)

pivotalTrials.title: Direct Transfer to an Endovascular Center vs Transfer to the Closest Local Stroke Center in Suspected Large Vessel Occlusion (RACECAT)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: In areas with a well-coordinated stroke system with rapid transfer, bypassing the local stroke-ready hospital to a distant thrombectomy center does NOT improve 90-day functional recovery (Class 3: No Benefit for bypass).

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Adjusted common OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.82–1.29; p=0.81; no functional benefit)

pico.population: Patients with anterior circulation LVO and large ischemic core defined as ASPECTS 3–5 on CT/MRI
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 6 hours or 6–24 hours with no change on FLAIR (ASPECTS 3–5)
pico.intervention: Endovascular thrombectomy + medical care

pivotalTrials.title: Endovascular Therapy for Acute Stroke with a Large Ischemic Region (RESCUE-Japan LIMIT)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: First landmark randomized trial proving that EVT significantly improves functional outcomes and reduces severe disability in patients with large core infarcts (ASPECTS 3–5).

primaryEndpoint.metric: mRS 0–3 at 90 days (functional independence / ambulatory survival)

pico.population: Patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis (≥60% on ultrasound) thought to require revascularization
pico.timeWindow: 5-year follow-up for primary prevention of stroke in asymptomatic carotid stenosis
pico.intervention: Carotid artery stenting (CAS)

pivotalTrials.title: Second Asymptomatic Carotid Surgery Trial (ACST-2): A Randomised Comparison of Carotid Artery Stenting versus Carotid Endarterectomy
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid stenosis, CAS and CEA offer equivalent procedural safety and long-term protection against stroke (Class 2a, LOE A in AHA/ASA 2024 Primary Prevention Guideline).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: Fatal or disabling procedural stroke: 1% in both groups
safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: 5-year overall stroke incidence: 5.3% in CAS vs. 4.5% in CEA (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.86–1.57)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Procedural death or any stroke within 30 days, or non-procedural fatal or disabling stroke at 5 years
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 2.5% vs. 2.5% (rate ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.64–1.51; p=0.91; identical long-term procedural and non-procedural stroke rates)

pico.population: Prehospital patients with suspected acute stroke dispatched by emergency call centers in Berlin
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4.5 hours from onset (hyperacute prehospital MSU)
pico.intervention: Mobile Stroke Unit (STEMO) dispatch

pivotalTrials.title: Effects of Mobile Stroke Unit Dispatch on Functional Outcomes in Patients with Suspected Acute Stroke (B_PROUD)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: MSU dispatch was associated with higher rates of IV thrombolysis (60% vs 48%), faster treatment initiation (median 20 min shorter), and reduced disability at 3 months.

primaryEndpoint.metric: mRS shift analysis across all disability grades at 3 months
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Adjusted common OR 1.21 (95% CI 1.01–1.44; p=0.04) in favor of MSU dispatch

pico.comparator: Standard EMS ambulance care to nearest hospital
pico.population: Suspected acute ischemic stroke patients eligible for tPA within 4.5h evaluated by prehospital EMS
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4.5 hours from onset (median 72 min to tPA on MSU)
pico.intervention: Mobile Stroke Unit (MSU) dispatch with onboard CT, lab, and tPA

pivotalTrials.title: Prospective, Multicenter, Controlled Trial of Mobile Stroke Units (BEST-MSU)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: MSUs accelerated median time to thrombolytic treatment by 36 minutes and resulted in significantly superior 90-day functional recovery, establishing MSUs as a preferred prehospital care model (Class 1, LOE A).

primaryEndpoint.metric: Utility-weighted mRS at 90 days in tPA-eligible cohort
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Mean score 0.72 vs. 0.66 (adjusted OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.75–3.36; p<0.001)

pico.comparator: Standard SBP target of 130 to 185 mm Hg for 24 hours
pico.population: AIS patients with anterior circulation LVO who achieved successful endovascular reperfusion (mTICI ≥2b)
pico.timeWindow: Within 1 hour post-successful reperfusion (intensive SBP 100–129 mmHg vs 130–180 mmHg)
pico.intervention: Intensive SBP target of 100 to 129 mm Hg for 24 hours post-procedure

pivotalTrials.title: Effect of Intensive vs Standard Blood Pressure Control on Intracerebral Hemorrhage After Successful Thrombectomy (BP-TARGET)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Targeting intensive SBP lowering to 100–129 mm Hg after successful mechanical thrombectomy does not reduce intracerebral hemorrhage or improve functional outcomes (ESO 2025 BP Guideline).

primaryEndpoint.metric: Rate of any radiographic intracranial hemorrhage on 24- to 36-hour CT
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 42.2% vs. 42.9% (adjusted OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.60–1.51; p=0.84; intensive BP reduction did not reduce hemorrhage)

pico.comparator: Clopidogrel (300 mg load, then 75 mg daily) + Aspirin for 21 days, then Clopidogrel monotherapy
pico.population: Patients with acute minor ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤3) or high-risk TIA (ABCD2 ≥4) carrying CYP2C19 loss-of-function (*2 or *3) alleles within 24h
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 24 hours from onset (CYP2C19 loss-of-function: Ticagrelor + ASA vs Clopidogrel + ASA)
pico.intervention: Ticagrelor (180 mg load, then 90 mg BID) + Aspirin for 21 days, then Ticagrelor monotherapy to day 90

pivotalTrials.title: Ticagrelor versus Clopidogrel in CYP2C19 Loss-of-Function Carriers with Minor Stroke or TIA (CHANCE-2)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: In minor stroke/high-risk TIA patients who carry CYP2C19 loss-of-function alleles, dual therapy with ticagrelor plus aspirin significantly reduced 90-day recurrent stroke compared to clopidogrel (Class 2b, LOE B-R).

primaryEndpoint.metric: New ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke within 90 days
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 6.0% vs. 7.6% (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.64–0.94; p=0.008; 23% relative risk reduction)

pico.comparator: Usual care (initial rate control, rhythm control only for unmanageable symptoms)
pico.population: Patients with early atrial fibrillation (diagnosed ≤1 year) and cardiovascular conditions / stroke risk
pico.timeWindow: Within 1 year of AF diagnosis (early rhythm-control therapy)
pico.intervention: Early rhythm-control therapy (antiarrhythmic drugs or catheter ablation)

pivotalTrials.title: Early Rhythm-Control Therapy in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation (EAST-AFNET 4)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Early rhythm control initiated within 1 year of AF diagnosis significantly reduces long-term stroke and cardiovascular mortality compared to rate control alone (Class 2a, LOE B-R in ACC/AHA 2023 AFib Guideline).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: No excess in major treatment-related complications (4.9% vs 1.4%)
safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: Stroke incidence: 0.6% vs 0.9% per year (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.44–0.97; 35% reduction in stroke)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Composite of death from cardiovascular causes, stroke, or hospitalization with worsening of heart failure or acute coronary syndrome
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 3.9% vs. 5.0% per year (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.66–0.94; p=0.005; 21% relative reduction in major cardiovascular events and stroke)

pico.population: Patients with mild-to-moderate AIS (NIHSS ≤5) or high-risk TIA (ABCD2 ≥6) presenting within 24h
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 24 hours from onset (minor AIS NIHSS ≤ 5 or high-risk TIA: Ticagrelor + ASA)
pico.intervention: Ticagrelor (180 mg load, then 90 mg BID) + Aspirin for 30 days

pivotalTrials.title: Ticagrelor and Aspirin or Aspirin Alone in Acute Ischemic Stroke or TIA (THALES)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Ticagrelor plus aspirin for 30 days significantly reduced 30-day stroke or death in mild stroke/TIA patients with a modest increase in bleeding risk (Class 2b, LOE B-R).

primaryEndpoint.metric: Composite of stroke or death within 30 days
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 5.5% vs. 6.6% (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.71–0.96; p=0.015; 17% relative reduction)

pico.population: Patients with acute major bleeding within 18 hours of taking factor Xa inhibitors (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, or enoxaparin); 64% with intracranial hemorrhage
pico.timeWindow: Acute presentation of life-threatening bleeding (within 18h of FXIa inhibitor intake)
pico.intervention: IV Andexanet alfa (bolus + 2-hour infusion)

pivotalTrials.title: Full Study Report of Andexanet Alfa for Factor Xa Inhibitor-Related Acute Major Bleeding (ANNEXA-4)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Andexanet alfa rapidly neutralizes factor Xa activity and achieves excellent-to-good hemostatic control in >80% of patients with life-threatening FXa-inhibitor ICH (Class 2a, LOE B-NR in 2022 ICH Guidelines).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: Hematoma expansion ≤35% achieved in 80% of evaluable ICH patients
safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: Thrombotic events occurred in 10% within 30 days; 30-day mortality was 14%

primaryEndpoint.metric: Excellent or good hemostatic efficacy at 12 hours + reduction in anti-factor Xa activity
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 82% achieved excellent or good hemostasis; anti-factor Xa activity decreased by 92% for apixaban and 92% for rivaroxaban (p<0.001)

pico.population: Children (≥2y) and adults with benzodiazepine-refractory convulsive status epilepticus
pico.timeWindow: Established Status Epilepticus (5 to 30 minutes of continuous seizure)
pico.intervention: IV Levetiracetam (60 mg/kg), Fosphenytoin (20 mg PE/kg), or Valproate (40 mg/kg)

pivotalTrials.title: Randomized Trial of Three Anticonvulsant Medications for Status Epilepticus (ESETT)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: High-dose IV Levetiracetam, Fosphenytoin, and Valproate are equally effective (~46%) as second-line agents for benzodiazepine-refractory status epilepticus.

safetyEndpoint.note: No statistically significant differences in life-threatening hypotension or intubation rates

primaryEndpoint.metric: Absence of clinically apparent seizures and improving responsiveness at 60 minutes
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Levetiracetam 47%, Fosphenytoin 45%, Valproate 46% (equivalent efficacy)

pico.population: AIS patients presenting between 4.5 and 9.0 hours from onset or wake-up stroke with automated perfusion mismatch (penumbra >10mL, mismatch ratio >1.2, core <70mL)
pico.timeWindow: 4.5 to 9.0 hours from onset or wake-up stroke (CTP/MRP mismatch)
pico.intervention: IV Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg

pivotalTrials.title: Thrombolysis Guided by Perfusion Imaging up to 9 Hours after Onset of Stroke (EXTEND)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Automated CT/MR perfusion mismatch allows safe extension of IV thrombolysis up to 9 hours or wake-up onset, significantly increasing the probability of mRS 0–1 (Class 2a, LOE B-R).

pico.population: Patients with non-traumatic spontaneous supratentorial ICH ≥30 mL with stable clot size at 6 hours
pico.timeWindow: 12 to 72 hours from symptom onset (stereotactic catheter evacuation + Alteplase irrigation)
pico.intervention: Image-guided catheter placement with stereotactic aspiration + alteplase (1.0 mg q8h for up to 9 doses)

pivotalTrials.title: Early Minimally Invasive Catheter Evacuation with Recombinant Tissue Plasminogen Activator in Patients with Spontaneous Intracerebral Haemorrhage (MISTIE III)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Minimally invasive catheter evacuation with thrombolytic irrigation is safe and reduces 30-day mortality; end-of-treatment residual hematoma <15 mL correlates with substantial functional gains (AHA 2022 ICH Guideline).

primaryEndpoint.metric: Good functional outcome (mRS 0–3 at 365 days / 1 year)
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 45% vs. 41% (adjusted hazard ratio 1.05, 95% CI 0.88–1.25; p=0.61; overall primary endpoint neutral, but post-hoc volume reduction to <15 mL improved outcomes)

pico.population: Adults with presumed acute stroke assessed within 4 hours by ambulance paramedics with SBP ≥120 mm Hg
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4 hours from symptom onset in the ambulance (prehospital GTN patch)
pico.intervention: Transdermal glyceryl trinitrate (GTN 5 mg patch applied immediately on-scene + daily for 3 days)

pivotalTrials.title: Prehospital Transdermal Glyceryl Trinitrate in Patients with Ultra-Acute Presumed Stroke (RIGHT-2): An Ambulance-Based, Randomised Trial
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Prehospital initiation of transdermal glyceryl trinitrate did not improve functional outcomes and demonstrated signals of potential harm; strictly NOT recommended (Class 3: Harm in AHA 2026).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: Death at 90 days: 17% in GTN vs. 15% in sham (p=0.48)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Shift in 90-day mRS score across all categories
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Adjusted common OR 1.25 (95% CI 0.97–1.60; p=0.08; no functional benefit, and trend toward worse disability in ICH and severe stroke subgroups)

pico.comparator: Standard glucose control with subcutaneous sliding-scale insulin targeting 80 to 179 mg/dL
pico.population: Hyperglycemic AIS patients presenting within 12h of stroke onset with blood glucose >110 mg/dL (diabetics) or ≥150 mg/dL
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 12 hours from symptom onset (intensive IV insulin target 80–130 mg/dL)
pico.intervention: Intensive glucose control with continuous IV insulin targeting 80 to 130 mg/dL for up to 72 hours

pivotalTrials.title: Effect of Intensive vs Standard Glucose Control on Functional Outcomes in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (SHINE)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Intensive glucose control to 80–130 mg/dL did not improve functional outcomes and significantly increased severe hypoglycemia. Intensive IV insulin target is NOT recommended (Class 3: No Benefit).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: Severe hypoglycemia (<40 mg/dL) occurred in 2.6% of intensive arm vs 0% of standard arm (p<0.001)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Favorable functional outcome (mRS adjusted for baseline stroke severity) at 90 days
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 15.7% vs. 16.2% (unadjusted relative risk 0.97, 95% CI 0.73–1.29; p=0.82; no clinical benefit)

pico.population: Community-dwelling healthy elderly (age ≥70 years, or ≥65 years among minorities) without cardiovascular disease, dementia, or disability
pico.timeWindow: Long-term primary prevention (median follow-up 4.7 years in healthy elderly)
pico.intervention: Enteric-coated Aspirin 100 mg daily

pivotalTrials.title: Effect of Aspirin on Disability-Free Survival and Major Hemorrhage in the Healthy Elderly (ASPREE)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Low-dose aspirin for primary prevention in healthy elderly people does not reduce stroke or prolong disability-free survival, while significantly increasing major hemorrhage and mortality; strongly NOT recommended (Class 3: Harm in AHA 2024 Primary Prevention Guideline).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: Intracranial hemorrhage: HR 1.38 (95% CI 1.03–1.86; p=0.03; major hemorrhage 8.6 vs 6.2 events per 1000 person-years; HR 1.38, p<0.001)
safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: All-cause mortality was higher in the aspirin group (12.7 vs 11.1 per 1000 person-years; HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.01–1.29)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Composite of death, dementia, or persistent physical disability
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 21.5 vs. 21.2 events per 1000 person-years (hazard ratio 1.01, 95% CI 0.92–1.11; p=0.79; zero benefit in disability-free survival)

pico.population: Anterior LVO (ICA/M1) with clinical-core mismatch (NIHSS ≥10 & small CTP/DWI core)
pico.timeWindow: 6 to 24 hours from last known well (including wake-up stroke; clinical-core mismatch)
pico.intervention: Thrombectomy + standard care

pivotalTrials.title: Thrombectomy 6 to 24 Hours after Stroke with a Mismatch between Deficit and Infarct (DAWN)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Establishes late-window (6–24h) mechanical thrombectomy as standard of care when clinical-core mismatch is present.

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: mRS 0–2: 49% vs. 13% (adjusted difference 33%, 95% CI 21–44; NNT = 2.8)

pico.population: Proximal MCA or ICA occlusion with initial infarct <70 mL and mismatch ratio ≥1.8 on CTP/MRI
pico.timeWindow: 6 to 16 hours from last known well (perfusion mismatch on CTP/MRP)
pico.intervention: Endovascular therapy + medical therapy

pivotalTrials.title: Thrombectomy for Stroke at 6 to 16 Hours with Selection by Perfusion Imaging (DEFUSE 3)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Perfusion-mismatch guided thrombectomy at 6–16 hours markedly improves functional outcomes and survival.

pico.population: AIS with ICA, M1,M2 or basilar occlusion eligible for IVT prior to EVT
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4.5 hours from symptom onset (bridging prior to EVT)
pico.intervention: IV Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg bolus before thrombectomy

pivotalTrials.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase before Thrombectomy for Ischemic Stroke (EXTEND-IA TNK)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg before EVT doubled early angiographic reperfusion and improved 90-day ordinal mRS compared with Alteplase.

primaryEndpoint.metric: Substantial reperfusion (>50% or absence of retrievable thrombus) at initial angiogram
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 22% vs. 10% (incidence diff 12%, p=0.002 for non-inferiority, p=0.03 for superiority)

pico.population: Minor AIS (NIHSS ≤3) or high-risk TIA (ABCD2 ≥4) within 12 hours
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 12 hours from symptom onset (minor AIS NIHSS ≤ 3 or high-risk TIA ABCD2 ≥ 4)
pico.intervention: Clopidogrel (600mg load, then 75mg/d) + Aspirin for 90 days

pivotalTrials.title: Clopidogrel and Aspirin in Acute Ischemic Stroke and High-Risk TIA (POINT)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: DAPT prevents early ischemic stroke recurrence, with benefit front-loaded in the first 21 days and bleeding risk rising thereafter.

safetyEndpoint.note: Major hemorrhage: 0.9% vs. 0.4% (HR 2.32, p=0.02; concentrated after day 21)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Major ischemic events (ischemic stroke, MI, or ischemic vascular death) at 90 days

pico.population: Patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting within 3h with mild non-disabling deficits (NIHSS 0–5)
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 3 hours from symptom onset (mild non-disabling AIS)
pico.intervention: IV Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg + oral placebo

pivotalTrials.title: Effect of Alteplase vs Aspirin on Functional Outcome for Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke and Mild Nondisabling Neurologic Deficits (PRISMS)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: In patients with acute mild non-disabling ischemic deficits, IV alteplase did not improve 90-day functional recovery and increased symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage; IVT is NOT recommended (Class 3: No Benefit).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: 3.2% vs. 0% (statistically significant increase in symptomatic hemorrhage with tPA; p=0.04)

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 78.2% vs. 81.5% (adjusted risk difference -1.1%, 95% CI -9.4% to 7.3%; p=0.79; no benefit with alteplase)

pico.population: Patients with acute ischemic stroke of unknown symptom onset or wake-up stroke with MRI DWI-FLAIR mismatch
pico.timeWindow: Unknown onset / wake-up stroke, ≤ 4.5h from symptom recognition (DWI-FLAIR mismatch)
pico.intervention: IV Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg

pivotalTrials.title: MRI-Guided Thrombolysis for Stroke with Unknown Time of Onset (WAKE-UP)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: In patients with wake-up stroke or unknown onset, MRI DWI lesion without marked FLAIR hyperintensity identifies salvageable tissue with significantly improved 90-day functional recovery after IV alteplase (Class 2a, LOE B-R).

pico.comparator: Standard IV nicardipine targeting SBP 140–179 mmHg
pico.population: Spontaneous supratentorial ICH (<60 mL) within 4.5h with initial SBP ≥180 mmHg
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 4.5 hours from symptom onset (intensive BP lowering target 110–139 mmHg)
pico.intervention: Aggressive IV nicardipine targeting SBP 110–139 mmHg

pivotalTrials.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage (ATACH-2)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Aggressive SBP reduction below 130 mmHg in acute ICH does not reduce death/disability and doubles renal adverse events.

safetyEndpoint.note: Renal adverse events within 7 days: 9.0% vs. 4.0% (p=0.002)

pico.population: Adults with acute spontaneous non-traumatic supratentorial ICH within 6 hours of onset while taking antiplatelet therapy (aspirin, clopidogrel, or dipyridamole) for ≥7 days
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 6 hours from symptom onset in antiplatelet-associated acute ICH (platelet transfusion harmful)
pico.intervention: Platelet transfusion initiated within 90 min of brain imaging

pivotalTrials.title: Platelet Transfusion versus Standard Care after Acute Stroke due to Spontaneous Cerebral Haemorrhage Associated with Antiplatelet Therapy (PATCH)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Platelet transfusion for acute ICH associated with antiplatelet therapy significantly increases the risk of death or severe disability and must NOT be administered (Class 3: Harm in AHA/ASA 2022 ICH Guidelines).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: In-hospital mortality: 24% in platelet group vs. 17% in standard care

primaryEndpoint.metric: Ordinal shift in mRS score (death or dependence) at 3 months
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Adjusted common OR 2.05 (95% CI 1.18–3.56; p=0.011; patients receiving platelets had DOUBLE the odds of worse functional disability or death)

pico.comparator: Usual stroke unit mobilization (typically starting 24–48 hours)
pico.population: Adult acute stroke patients admitted within 24 hours of onset
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 24 hours from onset (very early out-of-bed mobilization within 24h reduced good recovery)
pico.intervention: Very early mobilization (VEM: out-of-bed activity within 24h, high-frequency protocol)

pivotalTrials.title: Efficacy and Safety of Very Early Mobilisation within 24 h of Stroke Onset (AVERT)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: High-dose, very early out-of-bed mobilization within 24 hours of stroke onset is harmful and reduces the odds of favorable recovery. Out-of-bed mobilization should start between 24 and 48 hours (Class 3: Harm for <24h high-dose).

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 46% vs. 50% (adjusted OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.59–0.90; p=0.004; significantly worse outcome with high-dose VEM)

pico.population: AIS patients with proximal LVO, small ischemic core (ASPECTS 6–10), and moderate-to-good collaterals on multiphase CTA presenting within 12h
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 12 hours from symptom onset (good collaterals on multiphase CTA)
pico.intervention: Rapid endovascular thrombectomy + best medical therapy

pivotalTrials.title: Endovascular Treatment for Small Core and Anterior Circulation Proximal Occlusion with Emphasis on Minimizing CT-to-Groin Time (ESCAPE)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Rapid EVT guided by collateral CTA imaging up to 12 hours nearly doubled functional independence and cut mortality in half with an extraordinary NNT of 4 (Class 1, LOE A).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: 10.4% vs. 19.0% (statistically significant nearly 50% mortality reduction; p=0.04)

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 53.0% vs. 29.3% (rate ratio 1.80, 95% CI 1.34–2.42; p<0.001; absolute risk difference 23.7%, NNT=4)

pico.population: Adults with acute ischemic stroke and confirmed anterior circulation LVO presenting within 6 hours
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 6 hours from symptom onset
pico.intervention: Intraarterial treatment (thrombectomy with stent retrievers/aspiration) + usual care (IV tPA)

pivotalTrials.title: A Randomized Trial of Intraarterial Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke (MR CLEAN)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: First positive modern landmark RCT proving that endovascular mechanical thrombectomy is dramatically effective for anterior circulation LVO within 6 hours, launching the endovascular stroke era (Class 1, LOE A).

primaryEndpoint.metric: mRS shift analysis across all disability grades at 90 days
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: Adjusted common OR 1.67 (95% CI 1.21–2.30; p=0.002; absolute increase in functional independence mRS 0–2: 32.6% vs 19.1%, ARR 13.5%, NNT=7)

pico.population: Adults admitted with acute ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke within 24 hours of symptom onset
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 24 hours from stroke onset (preventive Ceftriaxone 2g daily for 4 days)
pico.intervention: Preventive IV Ceftriaxone (2 g once daily for 4 days)

pivotalTrials.title: Preventive Antibiotics in Stroke Study (PASS): A Pragmatic, Randomised, Open-Label Phase 3 Trial
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Routine prophylactic antibiotics reduced infections but did NOT improve functional independence or reduce mortality; routine preventive antibiotics are NOT recommended (Class 3: No Benefit in AHA 2026 & ESO 2026 SAP).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: 90-day mortality: 16.5% vs. 16.0% (p=0.74); infection rate reduced (11% vs 17%) without clinical gain

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 38.3% vs. 40.0% (adjusted common OR 0.95, 95% CI 0.82–1.11; p=0.55; no reduction in disability)

pico.comparator: Standard blood-pressure control targeting SBP <140 mm Hg
pico.population: Adults ≥50 years with SBP ≥130 mm Hg and high cardiovascular risk without diabetes or history of stroke
pico.timeWindow: Long-term primary prevention (median follow-up 3.26 years)
pico.intervention: Intensive blood-pressure control targeting SBP <120 mm Hg

pivotalTrials.title: A Randomized Trial of Intensive versus Standard Blood-Pressure Control (SPRINT)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Targeting SBP <120 mm Hg substantially reduces stroke, cardiovascular events, and all-cause mortality, forming the cornerstone of the AHA/ASA 2024 Primary Stroke Prevention guidelines (Class 1, LOE A).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: Serious adverse events (hypotension, syncope, acute kidney injury) were higher in intensive arm (4.7% vs 2.5%; p<0.001)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Composite of myocardial infarction, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 1.65% vs. 2.19% per year (hazard ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.64–0.89; p<0.001; 25% relative risk reduction; stroke HR 0.89, all-cause mortality HR 0.73, p=0.003)

pico.comparator: Standard stroke unit care without antibiotic prophylaxis
pico.population: Patients with acute stroke and dysphagia (failed bedside swallow screen) within 48h admitted to stroke units in the UK
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 48 hours from symptom onset in dysphagic stroke (preventive clarithromycin/co-amoxiclav)
pico.intervention: Clarithromycin + co-amoxiclav or cephalosporin for 14 days

pivotalTrials.title: Antibiotic Prophylaxis to Prevent Stroke-Associated Pneumonia (STROKE-INF): A Cluster-Randomised, Pragramtic Trial
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Antibiotic prophylaxis in dysphagic stroke patients did not reduce the frequency of pneumonia, 90-day mortality, or functional dependency; confirms lack of benefit (ESO 2026 SAP Guideline).

primaryEndpoint.metric: Post-stroke pneumonia in the first 14 days
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 13% vs. 10% (adjusted rate ratio 1.21, 95% CI 0.71–2.08; p=0.48; no reduction in stroke-associated pneumonia)

pico.comparator: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications for 7 days during acute phase
pico.population: Patients with acute ischemic stroke within 48 hours of onset and elevated SBP (140–220 mm Hg) not receiving IVT or EVT
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 48 hours from symptom onset (antihypertensive treatment in acute ischemic stroke)
pico.intervention: Immediate antihypertensive treatment to lower SBP by 10%–25% within 24h and target <140/90 within 7 days

pivotalTrials.title: Effects of Immediate Blood Pressure Reduction on Death and Major Disability in Patients with Acute Ischemic Stroke (CATIS)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: In patients with acute ischemic stroke and BP <220/120 mm Hg who do not receive reperfusion therapy, routine BP reduction does not prevent death or disability; antihypertensives should not be routinely initiated in the first 48–72h (Class 3: No Benefit in AHA 2026 & ESO 2025).

primaryEndpoint.metric: Death and major disability (mRS ≥3) at 14 days or hospital discharge

pico.comparator: Conservative intensive care medical therapy alone
pico.population: Patients >60 years of age with acute unilateral middle-cerebral-artery infarction involving ≥2/3 of territory with neurological deterioration
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 48 hours from onset (decompressive hemicraniectomy in elderly malignant MCA stroke)
pico.intervention: Hemicraniectomy within 48 hours of stroke onset

pivotalTrials.title: Hemicraniectomy for Massive Middle-Cerebral-Artery Infarction in Patients Older than 60 Years (DESTINY II)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Decompressive hemicraniectomy in malignant MCA infarction patients >60 years significantly reduces mortality from 70% to 33%, though most survivors live with substantial disability (mRS 4); recommended with shared decision-making (Class 2a, LOE B-R).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: Mortality dramatically reduced from 70% in conservative group to 33% in hemicraniectomy group (p<0.001)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Survival without severe disability (mRS 0–4) at 6 months
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 38% vs. 18% (odds ratio 2.91, 95% CI 1.06–7.49; p=0.04; significant survival advantage)

pico.population: Minor AIS (NIHSS ≤3) or high-risk TIA (ABCD2 ≥4) within 24 hours
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 24 hours from symptom onset (minor AIS NIHSS ≤ 3 or high-risk TIA ABCD2 ≥ 4)
pico.intervention: Dual antiplatelet therapy (Clopidogrel 300mg load then 75mg/d + Aspirin for 21 days)

pivotalTrials.title: Clopidogrel with Aspirin in Acute Minor Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (CHANCE)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Short-course 21-day DAPT (Clopidogrel + Aspirin) initiated within 24h of minor AIS or high-risk TIA reduces 90-day stroke recurrence by 32%.

primaryEndpoint.metric: Stroke recurrence (ischemic or hemorrhagic) at 90 days

pico.population: Immobile acute ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke patients admitted within 3 days
pico.timeWindow: Day 0–3 of acute stroke admission (intermittent pneumatic compression for DVT prevention)
pico.intervention: Thigh-length intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) applied for ≥30 days

pivotalTrials.title: Effectiveness of Intermittent Pneumatic Compression in Reduction of Risk of Deep Vein Thrombosis in Patients Who Have Had a Stroke (CLOTS 3)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) significantly reduces proximal DVT and 6-month mortality without bleeding risk in immobile stroke patients; highly recommended (Class 1, LOE A).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: Significant 14% relative reduction in 6-month mortality (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.72–0.99; p=0.042)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Occurrence of symptomatic or asymptomatic proximal DVT on compression Doppler ultrasound
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 8.5% vs. 12.1% (adjusted OR 0.65, 95% CI 0.51–0.84; p=0.001; absolute risk reduction 3.6%)

pico.population: Spontaneous ICH within 6h with elevated SBP (150–220 mmHg)
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 6 hours from symptom onset (intensive BP lowering SBP < 140 mmHg within 1h)
pico.intervention: Intensive BP lowering (target SBP <140 mmHg within 1 hour)

pivotalTrials.title: Rapid Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Acute Intracerebral Hemorrhage (INTERACT2)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Early smooth reduction of SBP toward 140 mmHg is safe and improves functional recovery scores in acute spontaneous ICH.

safetyEndpoint.sICH: Hematoma growth reduced; no excess severe hypotension

primaryEndpoint.metric: Death or major disability (mRS 3–6) & ordinal mRS shift at 90 days

pico.population: Patients with acute spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by a ruptured intracranial aneurysm assigned at admission
pico.timeWindow: Hyperacute aSAH admission (< 72 hours; coiling vs clipping)
pico.intervention: Endovascular coiling

pivotalTrials.title: The Barrow Ruptured Aneurysm Trial: 3-Year and 10-Year Outcomes Comparing Surgical Clipping versus Endovascular Coiling (BRAT)
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Coiling offers superior 1-year clinical recovery and lower perioperative morbidity, whereas clipping provides vastly superior long-term anatomical obliteration and lower retreatment rates (AHA/ASA 2023 aSAH Guideline).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: Retreatment rates: 16.4% in coiling vs. 1.2% in clipping over long-term follow-up
safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: 10-year mortality was comparable (29.6% clip vs 29.8% coil)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Poor functional outcome (mRS >2 at 1, 3, and 10 years)
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: At 1 year, poor outcome was 33.7% in clip vs 23.2% in coil (p=0.02); at 10 years, functional outcomes equilibrated between groups, but coil had higher aneurysm recurrence (15.4% vs 1.1%; p<0.001)

pico.population: Patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor for stroke
pico.timeWindow: Long-term secondary and primary stroke prevention (median 1.8 years)
pico.intervention: Apixaban (5 mg orally BID, or 2.5 mg BID for dose-reduction criteria)

pivotalTrials.title: Apixaban versus Warfarin in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation (ARISTOTLE)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Apixaban was superior to warfarin in preventing stroke or systemic embolism, caused 58% less intracranial hemorrhage, and resulted in lower all-cause mortality (Class 1, LOE A in ACC/AHA 2023 AFib Guideline).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: Intracranial hemorrhage: 0.33% vs. 0.80% per year (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.30–0.58; p<0.001; 58% reduction in ICH)
safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: All-cause mortality: 3.52% vs. 3.94% per year (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80–0.99; p=0.047)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke or systemic embolism
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 1.27% vs. 1.60% per year (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.69–0.91; p<0.001 for non-inferiority, p=0.01 for superiority; 21% relative reduction)

pico.population: Patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation and risk of stroke
pico.timeWindow: Long-term secondary stroke prevention in AF (median 2.0 years)
pico.intervention: Dabigatran 150 mg BID or 110 mg BID

pivotalTrials.title: Dabigatran versus Warfarin in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation (RE-LY)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: First landmark DOAC trial; dabigatran 150 mg was significantly superior to warfarin in reducing stroke with a massive 74% reduction in life-threatening intracranial bleeding (Class 1, LOE A).

safetyEndpoint.sICH: Life-threatening intracranial bleed: 0.10% vs. 0.38% (p<0.001; 74% reduction in ICH)

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 1.11% per year (150 mg) vs. 1.69% per year (warfarin) (relative risk 0.66, 95% CI 0.53–0.82; p<0.001 for superiority; 34% reduction in stroke)

pico.population: AIS patients presenting between 3.0 and 4.5 hours from symptom onset (excluding age >80y, severe stroke NIHSS >25, prior stroke + diabetes, or taking anticoagulants)
pico.timeWindow: 3.0 to 4.5 hours from symptom onset
pico.intervention: IV Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg

pivotalTrials.title: Thrombolysis with Alteplase 3 to 4.5 Hours after Acute Ischemic Stroke (ECASS III)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Established the expanded 3.0 to 4.5 hour therapeutic window for intravenous alteplase, demonstrating significant functional improvement without increasing overall mortality (Class 1, LOE A).

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 52.4% vs. 45.2% (odds ratio 1.34, 95% CI 1.02–1.76; p=0.04; absolute benefit 7.2%, NNT=14)

pico.population: Ruptured intracranial aneurysms (aSAH) anatomically suitable for both coiling and surgical clipping
pico.timeWindow: Acute aSAH admission (< 72 hours from rupture; endovascular coiling vs surgical clipping)
pico.intervention: Endovascular detachable platinum coiling

pivotalTrials.title: International Subarachnoid Aneurysm Trial (ISAT) of Neurosurgical Clipping versus Endovascular Coiling
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: For ruptured aneurysms amenable to both modalities, endovascular coiling yields superior 1-year survival free of disability compared with clipping.

safetyEndpoint.note: Lower 1-year disability and seizure risk with coiling; slightly higher late rebleeding rate

primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 23.7% vs. 30.6% (relative risk reduction 22.6%, absolute risk reduction 6.9%, p=0.0019)

pico.population: Patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting within 3 hours of symptom onset with no hemorrhage on CT
pico.timeWindow: ≤ 3 hours from symptom onset (0–180 min)
pico.intervention: IV recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg, max 90 mg; 10% bolus + 90% 1h infusion)

pivotalTrials.title: Tissue Plasminogen Activator for Acute Ischemic Stroke (The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke rt-PA Stroke Study)
pivotalTrials.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
pivotalTrials.bottomLine: Foundational landmark trial leading to the 1996 FDA approval of IV alteplase; proved that thrombolysis within 3 hours significantly increases the probability of disability-free survival despite a 6.4% sICH risk (Class 1, LOE A).

safetyEndpoint.mortality90d: 17% vs. 21% (p=0.30; no difference in overall mortality despite sICH)

primaryEndpoint.metric: Complete or near-complete neurological recovery at 3 months (favorable outcome on Barthel, mRS 0–1, GOS, NIHSS 0–1)
primaryEndpoint.resultStats: 39% vs. 26% across all global outcome scales (adjusted OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.2–2.6; p=0.008; absolute benefit 11%–13%, NNT=8)
